simple.meaning: מָאַר (mâʼar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be bitter or (causatively) to embitter , i.e. be painful.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Leviticus, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 13:51. The surrounding contexts include kingship, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָאַר (H3992) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָאַר (mâʼar) / H3992 is traced through Leviticus 13:51, Leviticus 13:52, Leviticus 14:44, Ezekiel 28:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: He shall examine the plague on the seventh day. If the plague has spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in the skin, whatever use the skin is used for, the plague is a destructive mildew. It is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, whether the warp or the woof, in wool or in linen, or anything of leather, in which the plague is, for it is a destructive mildew. It shall be burned in the fire.
then the priest shall come in and look; and behold, if the plague has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew in the house. It is unclean.
“ ‘ “There will be no more a pricking brier to the house of Israel, nor a hurting thorn of any that are around them that scorned them. Then they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”
